newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: ABB and Nat Grid finalists in Kazakh energy tender.
newsitem.headline: ABB and Nat Grid finalists in Kazakh energy tender.

text.p: Britain's National Grid Group and Sweden's ABB will find out late on Friday who has won rights to negotiate a deal to manage Kazakhstan's national power grid, a Kazakh energy source said on Thursday.

"This morning representatives of National Grid Group and Sweden's ABB -- the two finalists in the energy tender -- were invited to Prime Minister Akezhan Kazhegeldin's office and given the last few conditions to be met by 5 p.m. (1100 GMT) on Friday," the source told Reuters on condition of anonymity.

The source, who said the deal's conditions were confidential, said the government would choose one of the two companies on Friday evening, although tender results are often subject to delay in the former Soviet republic.
The tender announced on September 28 last year offered investors the right to manage the Central Asian state's power grid for 10-25 years.
"The sector is strategically important for the country's economy, so investors will have no right to have a stake in it," the source said.
The government of the resource-rich republic has provided no data on how much investment is needed.
